objective_for_doctor:
Age: 51
Sex: F
Chief Complaint: pain

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
I have a burning pain that starts in my stomach and goes up into my throat, sometimes with a bitter taste in my mouth. It gets worse after eating, and I also have a cough.
Can you tell me when the burning sensation started and whether it occurs at any particular time of day (e.g., after meals, at night, or when lying down)?
I don’t know. It gets worse after eating.
Does the burning improve when you take antacids, over‑the‑counter acid‑reducers, or when you sit upright after meals
I don’t know. But it does get worse after eating.
Do you notice any sour or acidic fluid coming back up into your mouth (regurgitation) or a feeling of food getting stuck when you swallow?
I don’t know.
Have you experienced any difficulty swallowing (a sensation that food is stuck), unintended weight loss, or chest pain that feels different from the burning?
I don’t know.
When did you first notice these symptoms, and have they been getting better, worse, or staying the same over time?
I don’t know.
Do you notice that the burning or cough gets worse when you lie down or go to bed after eating?
I don’t know. But it does get worse after eating.
Do you have any risk factors such as smoking, regular alcohol use, or frequent use of NSAIDs/aspirin?
Yes, I smoke cigarettes. I also have a hiatal hernia.
Do you experience frequent regurgitation of sour or bitter fluid into your mouth, especially after meals?
I don’t know. But I have a burning sensation that starts in my stomach and goes up into my throat, and it can be associated with a bitter taste in my mouth—especially worse after eating.
Do you have any hoarseness, a sore throat, or a sensation of a lump in your throat that comes on or worsens after meals?
I don’t know.
[DDX] Gastroesophageal reflux disease
